title: Japan national CPI (November 2026), 08:30 JST — a base-effect trough, and the last halving of the 2026 yearly-average band
source: EST: two independent Statistics Bureau surfaces, both re-fetched and parsed by this session on 2026-09-05. (1) stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes, the page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the row parses exactly as ['November', 'December 18', 'December', 'December 25', '2026 yearly average of Ku-area of Tokyo'] — i.e. the November-2026 national CPI releases 2026-12-18. (2) stat.go.jp/data/kouhyou/e-stat_cpi.xml, the Bureau's own machine-readable 公表予定 feed (HTTP 200, 59,990 bytes, UTF-16LE), linked from its live Japanese results page and NOT from the English schedule; its own update stamp is 2026-08-28, eight days before this fetch, and it reproduces all 30 release dates from the English table identically. Its 全国 class lists '2026-12-18 08:30 | 2026年11月分'. THE 08:30 JST RELEASE TIME IS NOW READ OFF A PRIMARY rather than asserted from convention (this entry previously stated the opposite): every one of the feed's 37 scheduled items carries release_hour 08 and release_minute 30. Filed estimate on two counts only — the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The third count this entry previously carried, that the schedule page has not been refreshed since 2026-01-23, is ANSWERED by surface (2) and is no longer a reason for the estimate label.
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2027-01-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Its own initial research (docs/research/events/japan-cpi-2026-12-18.md, same day) MEASURED the three inherited reasons for tracking it and revised all three; this note replaces the sweep's version. FIRST, and corrected: 'the print that fixes 11 of 12 months of the 2026 yearly average' is cumulative bookkeeping, not leverage. Every 2026 month weighs 1/12, so a +/-1.0pp y/y surprise HERE moves the 2026 annual rate by +/-0.083pp — identical to December's. The residual band for a common +/-1.0pp shock narrows +/-0.417 (5 months unknown) to +/-0.333 to +/-0.250 to +/-0.167 to +/-0.083 (after this print) to zero; it is already inside the Bureau's one-decimal rounding step by 2026-11-20, one print earlier. And the 2026 Japan yearly average does NOT publish here: the XML feed's class split lists 2026年平均 under 全国 on 2027-01-22 and under 東京都区部 on 2026-12-25, so the English row's Remarks cell belongs to the Tokyo release. This date publishes exactly one item, 2026年11月分. SECOND, and the finding that actually distinguishes it: this print is the trough of a base-effect V. On the Bureau's 2025-base national series (e-Stat statInfId=000040491314, parsed locally), the 2025 index path peaks in NOVEMBER — all-items 101.0, core 101.1, both the calendar-year high. Against the 2015-2024 seasonal norm that is a +0.30pp (all-items) / +0.28pp (core) HARD base for this y/y, reversing to -0.10pp / -0.23pp EASY for December's, while core-core's excess base is only +0.01pp. So a seasonally normal November delivers a 'Japan inflation slows' headline at 08:30 JST, roughly three hours before the same-day Bank of Japan decision (boj-decision-2026-12-18), on arithmetic rather than on any turn in underlying inflation. Registered as FT-japan-cpi-2026-12-18-1 at MEDIUM, because 2026's own monthly core-y/y changes have run -0.40/+0.20/-0.32/+0.10/0.00/+0.29pp and 0.28pp is one ordinary swing. THIRD: its content is pre-announced 21 days early by the Tokyo November flash on 2026-11-27 (tracked as japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-11-27), whose November-month gap to the national core print has a mean absolute size of 0.183pp and a worst month of 0.33pp over 2018-2025 — the tightest month measured on this calendar, on a sample of eight. So this date is THIRD in its own chain, behind 2026-11-27 for content and 2026-12-25 for the annual role. FOURTH, and downgraded: the sweep's claim that this is the LAST national release carrying a 2020-base companion is UNSUPPORTED rather than settled. It rests entirely on one English sentence ('The 2020-base CPI will also be calculated and released until December 2026', stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/2025plan.html) read as calendar time; the Bureau's release feed lists no 2020-base publication item at any point from 2026-08-21 through 2027-03-26, but that is argument-from-absence because a companion table is not a separately scheduled release. Registered as FT-japan-cpi-2026-12-18-3 at LOW, with a free checkpoint on 2026-09-18. FIFTH, unchanged and re-verified: this is one of six Friday-concluding BoJ decisions that share their date with a Bureau CPI release (0 of 4 non-Friday decisions do) — already covered by FT-japan-cpi-2027-01-22-3, which counts this date as one of its checkpoints, so it is not re-registered here. The BoJ's own table shows '-' in the Outlook Report column for the December MPM. Impact stays LOW: symbols is empty and no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI. Attribution hazard worth carrying: 13 tracked events sit within +/-5 days and this date also carries opex-2026-12-18 (triple witching, high, confirmed) and intl-transactions-q3-2026-12-18, so a US tape move on 2026-12-18 has at least three better explanations than Japan's November CPI.
